key_insight: The paper makes operator learning self-explainable by rewriting predictions as localized integral contributions, so specific input regions can be directly linked to output patterns.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers an interpretable way to trust and diagnose surrogate models for fluid-flow problems such as blood flow and unsteady aerodynamics.
method: Reformulate operator learning as generalized functional linear models with integral equations.
Split the input domain into subdomains and compute local integrals to measure regional contribution.
Use the resulting decomposition to map spatial features in the input to prediction-relevant output patterns.
evidence_signal: The framework is demonstrated on function-to-scalar and function-to-function fluid-flow tasks, and the identified important regions align qualitatively with established post-hoc explainability methods.
watch_item: The approach relies on a chosen domain decomposition, so explanation quality may depend on how subdomains are defined and may need careful tuning for complex geometries.
paper_title: Self-explainable Operator Learning for Discovering Spatial Patterns in Functional Data
